title: SIR Maharashtra: Preliminary Report (2026)
shows: From the lists of names left off Maharashtra's draft roll for all 288 constituencies, the Sabar Institute counts 2,06,88,421 names, 21.1% of the 9,78,54,049 electors on the roll before the revision, and finds 16.8% of them marked dead. It describes the other 1,72,06,190, marked permanently shifted, untraceable or absent, or already enrolled elsewhere, as alive. It reports that Mumbai's 36 constituencies have 11% of the state's electors and 17% of the names, that in Colaba more names were left off than votes were cast in 2024, and that names left off for a reason other than death exceed the 2024 winning margin in 190 of the 288 seats. It finds 3,250 of the 6,101 third gender electors on the 2024 roll, 53.3%, on the lists. Outside Mumbai, among electors aged 18 to 29 marked permanently shifted, it counts 8,22,798 women and 3,79,991 men, which it reads as consistent with women moving to a husband's home after marriage. The roll has no column for religion, and Sabar classifies the names by religion itself. By that classification Muslim names are 14.6% of the names left off, against about 12.1% expected from the 2011 Census, and the odds of a Muslim name being marked already enrolled elsewhere are 2.07 times those of other names of the same age in the same seat. The report says this does not show that anyone was targeted, and that name matching may explain part of it. It finds no difference between the seats of the two alliances once Mumbai, region, reservation, urbanisation and size are allowed for, and the strongest link is with low turnout in 2024. The office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer replied on 7 November that electors marked dead or already enrolled are a little over 25% of the names and those marked absent or shifted about 75%, that comparing Mumbai and Thane with the state average is not appropriate, and that the revision is still under way, PTI reported.
quote: Deaths account for only 16.8% of deletions.
Non-death deletions exceed the 2024 winning margin in 190 of 288 seats.
note: First reading, 8 November 2026. The report's page (dated November 7, 2026) read through a rendering scrape, since the site draws its pages in the browser, and the report itself (SIR_Maharashtra_Preliminary_Report_SABAR.pdf, 305 pages, from the page's download link) read with pdftotext, the state-wide pages 1 to 16 in full. Its 9,78,54,049 electors before the revision agree with the site's figure for Maharashtra. Its 2,06,88,421 names are 66 fewer than the site's 2,06,88,487 left off the draft, and the report says 66 rows in Mumbadevi are missing from the Commission's own PDFs and that 51 of 1,00,216 polling parts have no published report. Colaba is 1,19,606 names against 1,18,499 votes in 2024 by its table. The two quotes are verbatim from the executive summary. The odds ratio compares a Muslim name with other names for already enrolled against death. The Chief Electoral Officer's reply is PTI's report in Vartha Bharati (datePublished 2026-11-07T23:42:24+05:30), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl, which gives it as a reply to the Sabar survey. Clarion India's report of the study (2026-11-07T13:12:24+05:30) was read beside it. The report's figures on women of 49.8% of the living names and its correlations by district and caste composition are not carried. The report's view of what the deletions mean for elections is its own.
